acceptanceCriteria: Recognizably belongs to the Great Cats family and preserves every identity invariant.
Reads specifically as Lynx, T2, rather than another family form.
Communicates the High-Ground Soldier archetype and its battlefield duty.
Preserves coherent load-bearing anatomy, complete limbs, and believable ground contact.
Uses at least two wind construction dimensions without a palette-only or glow-only treatment.
Keeps the attack telegraph and counterplay signal visible at gameplay scale.
Frames one complete featured subject with no crop, labels, UI text, or watermark.
Output remains a candidate until independent approved-review evidence exists; it is never a runtime asset.
anatomyInvariants: Larger compact cat with long hind legs, short tail, broad facial ruff, and oversized snowshoe paws.
Signature mechanic: Perch Exchange: the Lynx uses two visible perches and must complete one grounded pause after each attack.
battlefieldDuty: Bound between raised perches and attack whichever target presents the longest exposed back.
constructionDimensions: Fur, mane, ear tufts, and tail edges stretch into directional filaments while the core body remains opaque.
Pressure wakes and cover movement trace leaps, silent lanes, and territory boundaries with precise direction.
counterplay: Rotate toward the perch or vacate the cone, then punish the grounded pause. Affinity signal: The moving pressure sheath collapses at the still eye line, landing shoulder, or planted canine after commitment.
forbiddenTreatments: Omnidirectional turbulence that hides pounce or sightline geometry
identityInvariants: Every form retains a four-legged feline body, flexible spine, retractile claws, whiskered muzzle, mobile ears, and expressive tail.
Species variation remains feline and is communicated by coat pattern, limb proportion, mane, canine length, and hunting posture rather than equipment.
Eye line, tail stillness, shoulder compression, cover disturbance, and landing posture preserve readable attack direction.
telegraph: Ear tufts flatten and the selected perch sheds dust toward its landing cone.
